accepted.question_text: For a preemptive uniprocessor real-time system modeled as a finite sporadic task system tau = {tau_1, ..., tau_n}, where each task tau_i has worst-case execution time C_i, relative deadline D_i, and period T_i, generates jobs at least T_i time units apart, and each generated job requires at most C_i execution and has deadline D_i time units after its arrival, determine the computational complexity of deciding fixed-priority schedulability in the implicit-deadline case D_i = T_i for every task. The input includes a specified total priority order on the tasks, and fixed-priority scheduling always executes an incomplete job of the highest-priority task. Is tau schedulable under that specified priority order, meaning that all deadlines are met for every legal sequence of job arrivals?

evidence.quote: A sporadic task τiis characterized by three parameters — a worst-case execution time Ci, a relative deadline Di, and a period Ti.
For a given scheduling algorithm A, τ is said to be A-schedulable if algorithm A meets all deadlines when scheduling every collection of job arrivals that may legally be generated by τ .

Problem 1 (Computational complexity of FP schedulability analysis – implicit deadline tasks.) What is the computational complexity of the following problem? Input: Implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ, with a specified priority assignment on (a total ordering of) the tasks in τ. Question: Is τ FP-schedulable with the specified priority assignment?

accepted.question_text: For a preemptive uniprocessor real-time system modeled as a constrained-deadline sporadic task system tau, where each task tau_i = (C_i, D_i, T_i) has relative deadline D_i no larger than its period T_i, determine whether there exists a pseudo-polynomial-time algorithm for deciding Earliest Deadline First schedulability. Earliest Deadline First scheduling always executes the pending job with the earliest deadline, and tau is EDF-schedulable when EDF meets all deadlines for every legal sequence of job arrivals. The source records that weak coNP-hardness is known, leaving the pseudo-polynomial-time decision question open.

evidence.quote: The Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling algorithm schedules at each instant in time the job currently awaiting execution that has the earliest deadline.

Problem 2 (Computational complexity of uniprocessor EDF-schedulability analysis – constrained-deadline tasks.) What is the computational complexity of the following problem? Input: Constrained-deadline sporadic task system τ Question: Is τ EDF-schedulable?

Progress since Dagstuhl. Problem 2 was shown to be weakly coNP-hard by Eisenbrand and Rothvoß in [9]. The outstanding open question is thus whether a pseudo-polynomial time algorithm exists for problem 2.

accepted.question_text: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system under global scheduling, determine the computational complexity of feasibility analysis for sporadic task systems with arbitrary deadlines. The input is a sporadic task system tau and a positive integer m > 1; global scheduling permits a job to begin execution on any processor and to resume on any processor after preemption. Is tau feasible on a platform of m preemptive processors, meaning that for every legal sequence of job arrivals generated by tau there exists a schedule meeting all deadlines?

evidence.quote: In global scheduling, by contrast, a job may begin execution on any processor, and a preempted job may resume execution upon any processor.

Problem 3 (Multiprocessor global feasibility analysis – arbitrary-deadline tasks) Input: Sporadic task system τ . A positive integer m > 1. Question: Is τ feasible upon a platform comprised of m preemptive processors (under the global scheduling paradigm)?

For constrained-deadline and arbitrary-deadline systems, however, no algorithms – of any computational complexity whatsoever– are known; thus, the computational complexity of this problem remains wide open for such systems.

accepted.question_text: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system under global Earliest Deadline First scheduling, determine an exact decision procedure or computational complexity for EDF schedulability of implicit-deadline sporadic task systems. The input is an implicit-deadline sporadic task system tau, in which each task has D_i = T_i, and a positive integer m > 1; the question is whether global EDF meets every deadline for every legal sequence of job arrivals on a platform of m preemptive processors.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Exact multiprocessor global EDF-schedulability — implicit-deadline tasks.) Input: Implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ . A positive integer m > 1. Question: Is τ EDF-schedulable upon a platform comprised of m preemptive processors?

Sufficient EDF-schedulability tests are known; for instance, it is known that any implicit-deadline task system τ satisfying U(τ ) ≤ m − (m − 1) × maxτi∈τ{Ci/Ti} is EDF-schedulable on an m-processor platform
It is easy to see that the above condition is not exact

accepted.question_text: For a preemptive multiprocessor real-time system with implicit-deadline sporadic tasks and a specified total priority order on the tasks, determine whether global fixed-priority schedulability is decidable by an exact test and what its computational complexity is. The input is tau, m > 1 preemptive processors, and the priority assignment; the question is whether fixed-priority scheduling on m processors meets every deadline for every legal job-arrival sequence generated by tau.

evidence.quote: In fixed-priority (FP) scheduling, each task in τ is assigned a unique priority. All the task priorities are totally ordered
Problem 4 (Exact multiprocessor global EDF-schedulability — implicit-deadline tasks.) Input: Implicit-deadline sporadic task system τ . A positive integer m > 1.
The analog of Problem 4 with respect to FP scheduling — Given τ, m, and a priority assignment, is τ FP-schedulable on m processors under the given priority assignment? — is also open.

accepted.question_text: For multiprocessor scheduling of sporadic task systems whose task parameters C_i, D_i, and T_i are all positive integers, determine whether the Integer Boundary Constraint holds. That is, is a sporadic task system feasible on a multiprocessor platform under continuous preemptive scheduling if and only if, for every legal sequence of job arrivals, there exists a discrete schedule that divides time into indivisible time slots and assigns tasks to slots while meeting all deadlines?

evidence.quote: Suppose that all task parameters – the Ci’s, Di’s, and Ti’s – of a sporadic task system are specified as positive integers.
A discrete schedule assumes that the time-line is divided into indivisible time-lots, and specifies the tasks scheduled during each time-slot.

Problem 5 (Does the Integer Boundary Constraint (IBC) hold for multiprocessors?) Is it true that a sporadic task system is multiprocessor feasible if and only if it has a discrete schedule for every sequence of job arrivals?
